name: 青腳鷸
illustrationTaxon: Tringa nebularia, monotypic: 30-35 cm. An elegant wader with a slightly upturned, fairly broad-based bill and longish green or grey-green legs, generally greyish with white underparts. The adult winter is paler and greyer with more extensive white on the underparts, while the juvenile is darker above with neat pale fringes to the upperparts and fine streaking on the chest and upper flanks. In flight the white tapers from the uppertail coverts to a point on the mantle at approximately the leading edge of the wing, the tail feathers are lightly barred and usually darker on the central feathers, the wings are plain and the legs project beyond the tail.

similarSpecies.distinction: 澤鷸體型明顯更小更瘦，嘴細長而筆直、不上翹，腿相對更長更細而呈暗綠灰色，頸長而頭小；本種嘴較粗厚、微微上翹，體型大一截、身型也較結實。
小青腳鷸身型矮壯、腿短而偏黃（本種腿長而綠），嘴更粗厚而兩色分明，繁殖期胸腹佈滿黑色圓斑；本種腿長、嘴較細而微微上翹，胸腹沒有圓斑。

featureNotes: 嘴基部頗寬，往尖端微微上翹——這是把牠和嘴細直如針的澤鷸分開的第一眼特徵（第1圈取自近景圖，實際可見）。
深色眼先之上是一條長而清楚的白眉，頭頂、後頸至頸側則佈滿細密縱紋，遠看像一件直條紋的襯衫（第2圈取自近景圖，實際可見）。
背中央有一道白色楔形，由尾上覆羽向前收窄到肩部；飛行時這道白色正好和翅膀的素淨深色形成對比（第3圈取自全身圖，實際可見）。
腿長而呈青綠或灰綠色——中文名「青腳」由此而來；腿伸出尾後，站姿高挺（第4圈取自全身圖，實際可見）。

sources.use: HKBWS substantive read: Category I, an abundant passage migrant and common winter visitor to the Deep Bay area with scattered records elsewhere, also a scarce summer visitor; 30-35 cm, an elegant wader with a slightly upturned fairly broad-based bill and longish green or grey-green legs, generally greyish with white underparts, the adult winter being paler and greyer with more extensive white on the underparts and the juvenile darker above with neat pale fringes to the upperparts and fine streaking on the chest and upper flanks; in flight the white tapers from the uppertail coverts to a point on the mantle at approximately the leading edge of the wing, the tail feathers are lightly barred and usually darker on the central feathers, the wings are plain and the legs project beyond the tail; the typical flight call is a ringing distinctive tyoo uttered 2-5 times; most records are from the intertidal mudflats of Deep Bay and adjacent roosting areas primarily at Mai Po NR, also regularly recorded at Long Valley where the highest count is eight, up to 17 in freshwater habitats in the Kam Tin area, and surprisingly rare on Lantau, with elsewhere scattered coastal localities throughout the New Territories generally singly or in groups of up to eight apart from 40 migrating over the sea south of HK Island on 24 April 1994 and 26 at Luk Keng on 1 May 2009; apparent migrants are first noted during the first half of July with numbers peaking around the third week of September and the wintering population probably established by mid-November, the highest autumn count being 1,816 on 22 August 2006, autumn counts rising to a peak in 2006 before falling to a low in 2019; the peak count of wintering birds generally numbered no more than 400 until winter 2002/03, then increased to whole Deep Bay peaks of over 1,500 from winter 2006/07 to 2008/09 (highest 1,717 on 21 December 2008) with the highest on the HK side being 1,489 on 13 January 2008, and since then peak counts have been substantially lower, mostly up to 800; spring migrants are probably present in the first week of March with the main passage lasting from the last week of March to the second week of May and peaking in the first week of the latter month, the highest count being 1,918 on 19 April 2008, peak spring counts rising to a peak in 2008 before falling to a low in 2017 and 2018, and up to 136 birds recorded in June and early July in Deep Bay; one bird ringed at Mai Po was shot in central Siberia; Vaughan and Jones (1913) called it a common winter visitor arriving on 21st or 22nd September and leaving between 3 March and 1 April; it pecks and probes in shallow water at a consistent pace but may also run quickly with sudden sharp changes of direction when opportunistically exploiting prey abundance, has been observed predating mudskippers greater than its bill length, and has been recorded on nocturnal migration over Sai Kung; monotypic, breeding between approximately 50 and 70 degrees north from Scandinavia east through Russia and northern Kazakhstan to Kamchatka and wintering in coastal north and sub-Saharan Africa, the Middle East, the Indian subcontinent and south China south through Indochina, southeast Asia and Indonesia to Australia; in China a migrant through much of the country and a winter visitor from the Yangtze floodplain south to the coast including Hainan and Taiwan; IUCN Least Concern with a stable population trend.

notes: AI 生成插圖，經人眼核對微微上翹而基部較寬的嘴、白眉與頭頸縱紋、背中央的白色楔形及青綠色長腿；單型種。
兩隻比較鳥均為 AI 生成示意（澤鷸、小青腳鷸，本卡新繪製並已核對），非等比例；卡上不作完整鑑別檢索表。
插圖取非繁殖羽偏灰的樣貌（冬季較淡較灰、腹部白色更多），與本種在香港以過境及越冬為主的出現時間相符。
飛行時白色由尾上覆羽向前收窄到肩部、尾羽有淡橫斑且中央較深、雙腳伸出尾後——這些要在飛行中才看得清，卡面只放靜態站姿。
地圖為 Natural Earth 110m 世界底圖的國家層級概述，不是精確分佈多邊形，繁殖地與越冬地不分工。
IUCN 無危 LC（趨勢穩定）；香港屬 Category I，屬常見的過境鳥與后海灣一帶的常見越冬鳥，數量在 2006–2008 年見高峰後回落。
本卡順帶預告下一張的小青腳鷸 *Tringa guttifer*（EN）尚未交付，該鳥在港屬稀少過境鳥。
只交付 aviandex/0167.avif 單一檔案到指定 Drive 資料夾，不壓縮成 ZIP。
